summary: Updates RFC 1229, RFC 1230, RFC 1231, RFC 1232 and RFC 1233 with new codes when MIBs move from experimental to standard assignments. It is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo moves five management information bases (MIBs) from experimental identifiers to standard identifiers. It recommends assigning standard identifiers early so implementations do not need a late change.

questions: why were experimental mib codes reassigned
subtitle: Moves five MIB assignments from the experimental namespace to standard namespaces.

tldr.problem: Assigning standard MIB identifiers only late in standardization could force implementation changes and create operational problems.
tldr.mechanism: The memo assigns new standard object identifier arcs to five MIBs and recommends assigning standard arcs early and preserving them.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1239 is Historic and updates RFCs 1229 through 1233 with the listed codes.

today: RFC 1239 is Historic and updates RFC 1229, RFC 1230, RFC 1231, RFC 1232 and RFC 1233. The unit metadata records no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: Why the Assignments Changed
sections.content:
Previously, a MIB could receive an experimental namespace arc early and wait until Full Standard status for an arc in the standard namespace. The memo says this could make vendors revise implementations without a substantive technical change, create late operational problems and discourage implementation before Full Standard status.

It recommends assigning an arc in the standard MIB namespace at the earliest phase of standardization and preserving that assignment as the standard progresses.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing identifiers late can force vendors to revise working implementations. The memo recommends using the standard identifier from an early stage and keeping it.

sections.title: The Five MIBs Covered
sections.content: RFC 1239 updates RFCs 1229, 1230, 1231, 1232 and 1233 with new codes. The affected objects cover generic interface extensions, IEEE 802.4 Token Bus, IEEE 802.5 Token Ring, DS1/T1 Carrier and DS3. The memo says future code assignments should be checked in each MIB publication.
sections.plainLanguage: The reassignment covers five MIBs for interfaces and transmission technologies. The memo directs readers to each publication for later code assignments.

sections.title: Experimental and Standard Prefixes
sections.content:
The old experimental prefix is 1.3.6.1.3. The new standard assignments use prefix 1.3.6.1.2.1 for Generic IF code 12, and the transmission prefix 1.3.6.1.2.1.10 for IEEE 802.4 code 8, IEEE 802.5 code 9, DS1 code 18 and DS3 code 30. The memo's table also lists the old codes under the experimental prefix.

The memo states that security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC gives old experimental codes and their new standard prefixes and codes. It does not discuss security issues.
